summary: 4 verified, 7 corrected, 3 removed, 1 personal-ok · Needs review: SR 26-2 was verified only through secondary sources (law-firm and vendor summaries). Please check the primary text on federalreserve.gov. Several secondary sources say SR 26-2 may carve generative or agentic AI out of model-risk scope. The article makes no claim either way, so confirm the scope before adding one.; The FTC figure is for 2024. FTC data for 2025 may already have been published (the FTC announced 2025 fraud data in early 2026). Consider whether the hook and opening should use the newer figures.; The four 'should not' lines and the three LinkedIn rules are now written as recommendations. Ajay Kant should confirm whether they match his actual practice at L&T Finance before wording them as 'I do'.; The 'Ji et al.' myth/fact is worded in general terms. Check that it matches how the survey defines hallucination before publishing.

checks.claim: FTC: consumers reported losing more than $12.5 billion to fraud in 2024
checks.note: FTC press release, 10 March 2025. The draft's source URL was malformed (12-5 instead of 125) and has been fixed.

checks.claim: 2024 losses were up 25% on 2023; 2023 losses were about $10 billion
checks.note: FTC: 25% rise, and 2023 was the first year losses topped $10 billion. Wording changed to 'more than $10 billion' / 'more than $12.5 billion'.
FTC press release. Removed the unsupported line 'fraud volumes are growing faster than most analytics teams'.

checks.claim: Ji et al. (2023), ACM Computing Surveys, on hallucination in NLG
checks.note: ACM Computing Surveys 55(12), Article 248, published online March 2023. The statement was reworded to 'fluent text that is wrong or unfaithful to its source'.

checks.claim: SR 11-7 defines 'model' broadly and applies as current US guidance
checks.note: SR 11-7 was replaced by SR 26-2 on 17 April 2026 (Fed/FDIC/OCC). The article and Myth/Fact item were rewritten. SR 26-2 is described by secondary sources as keeping effective challenge and independent review.

checks.claim: Myth/Fact: 'SR 11-7 applies only to credit scoring models'
checks.note: Replaced with a verifiable item: SR 11-7 was superseded by SR 26-2 on 17 April 2026.
Central Bank of Ireland; ESMA also confirms the 17 January 2025 application date.

checks.claim: Fraud analyst hiring is slow and good analysts are scarce
checks.note: No source found. Replaced with a neutral statement that analytics capacity is finite.

checks.claim: 'Every fraud team I know…' and the direction 'is familiar to anyone in a bank's fraud team'
checks.note: Not in the profile or verifiable. Reworded to a general observation and a 'useful signal of direction'.

checks.claim: I treated logging and human review as part of the design from day one
checks.note: The profile says only that the agent runs with logging and human review. 'From day one' is not supported.

checks.claim: 'I keep four lines clear' and 'three things I hold to' (author's operating practice)
checks.note: The profile does not state these practices. Reframed as recommendations ('I would', 'should'). The title was changed to 'I'd let / wouldn't'.

checks.claim: Freed time was redirected to detection and drove the 20% uplift
checks.note: The profile does not link the agent's time savings to the uplift. Reworded to a programme-level result.

checks.claim: Illustrative maths: 11.25 hours a week, 517 hours a year, 0.3 FTE; 'a few weeks of analyst time'
checks.note: Arithmetic checks out (40×0.5×45×0.75/60 = 11.25; ×46 = 517.5; ÷1,800 ≈ 0.29). 517 hours is about 13 working weeks, not 'a few weeks', so the wording was corrected. The 46 weeks and 1,800 hours are now labelled as assumptions.

checks.claim: At L&T Finance: built Fraud Risk Analytics team from scratch and an LLM-based agent for routine analytics, with logging and human review; early-detection +20%
checks.note: Supported by the PROFILE (experience and quick answers).

checks.claim: 'I have no published figure for hours saved'
checks.note: Reworded to 'no measured hours-saved figure behind this article', which makes no claim about the author.
